assumptions: Only placeholders of the currently configured names are preserved, never any <secret:...>-shaped text: a looser shape would let failure text such as '<secret:note VALUE>' hide a configured value from redaction (pinned by a test). Residual: if the two passes use different CANARY_INGEST_REDACT_ENV name sets, a pass-1 placeholder whose name is not configured on pass 2 is not protected; no value can leak from that, only garbling.
When two configured names share one value, the first in longest-first order names it, which matches the old sequential behaviour.
Literal text in a failure that already reads <secret:...> is left as is; it is a placeholder shape, not a credential.
Closes #1400 because part 1 merged in #1430 and this PR adds the issue's second done-when test (a double pass where the value is a substring of its own placeholder).

fc1026b: 'a value beats a placeholder it overlaps' is applied to every overlap shape, not only start-inside/end-outside: a value starting before a placeholder and ending inside it, or containing it, also unprotects it (this matches the earlier leftmost-match behaviour for those shapes).

fc1026b: overlapping occurrences of values (including a value overlapping itself, e.g. 'aaaaaa' in 'aaaaaaa') merge into one <secret:NAME> span named by the leftmost, then longest, value. Previously a leftmost non-overlapping match could leave a partial fragment; now strictly more text is redacted.
fc1026b: a straddled placeholder is broken (e.g. 'x <secret:TO<secret:TOK> y'), matching main's pre-PR output for the same input; garbling is accepted over leaking.
fc1026b: the overlap check uses sorted spans and prefix reaches (O(n log n)); a first pairwise draft took ~2.4 s on 40k repeated placeholders, so a timing guard test pins it.
